summary: The joke that it is horror about "hang out with Australians" lands because the movie is all sweaty social pressure. It feels like being trapped in bad company until the whole world turns hostile and unreal.
good_pick_if: you want something tense, ugly, and impossible to shake off
maybe_skip_if: you want your thrillers less abrasive or less boozy

source_quotes.text: what if you had to hang out with Australians

summary: The "no horns, just a hoodie" line gets why this hits so hard. It takes revenge-thriller intensity and makes it feel modern, brutal, and sickeningly intimate instead of mythic or fun.
good_pick_if: you want an extreme thriller with real velocity and menace
maybe_skip_if: graphic cruelty or nihilism is a hard no

source_quotes.text: He had no horns, just a hoodie.

summary: One reviewer just calls it "one of the best love stories ever shown on film," and that is the real lane. The horror is great, but the deeper pull is the lonely winter tenderness underneath it.
good_pick_if: you want something eerie, intimate, and unexpectedly gentle
maybe_skip_if: you want your vampire movies campier or more openly pulpy

source_quotes.text: one of the best love stories ever shown on film

summary: Calling it a "stylish erotic thriller" barely covers it. The movie is tight, sexy, funny, and so in control of its own mechanics that every switch in allegiance feels like part of the seduction.
good_pick_if: you want a slick thriller with chemistry and actual confidence
maybe_skip_if: you want less pulp or less heat in your crime movies

summary: The "I bet Hitchcock wished he made this" reaction makes sense. It is elegant, nasty, and weirdly self-aware, with a voyeuristic chill that feels both classic and ahead of its time.
good_pick_if: you want old-school horror with craft and real creep factor
maybe_skip_if: you want slashier thrills than slow-burn discomfort

summary: The best review angle is that this Batman finally "looks for clues in a big stack of dusty old files." It leans fully into detective noir, rain-soaked grime, and brooding immersion instead of superhero quippiness.
good_pick_if: you want Batman as a moody mystery more than a quip machine
maybe_skip_if: you want lighter comic-book energy or tighter pacing

summary: That "what’s your favourite scary movie" line is still the hook because the movie is playful, sharp, and deeply crowd-friendly. It gets the slasher mechanics and still has fun messing with them.
good_pick_if: you want horror that is tense, funny, and easy to watch with friends
maybe_skip_if: you want your slashers played completely straight

summary: People quote "not many people have basements in California" because the movie makes ordinary details feel catastrophic. It is procedural obsession turned into dread, with tension that just keeps quietly tightening.
good_pick_if: you want a meticulous thriller that earns every shiver
maybe_skip_if: you want closure, speed, or emotional relief

summary: One smart description calls it "an existential play disguised as a thriller," which is why people lock into it. The movie moves like noir, but the real appeal is the mood, drift, and uneasy male chemistry.
good_pick_if: you want a thriller that cares more about atmosphere than payoff
maybe_skip_if: you want cleaner plotting or faster suspense beats

summary: Calling it an "epic, memorable, violent, engrossing" saga is about right. It is big-hearted and bruising at once, with family loyalty and neighborhood identity giving the whole crime story real weight.
good_pick_if: you want a long crime story powered by loyalty and cultural texture
maybe_skip_if: you want something leaner or less melodramatic
